"After plenty of pleading, Judy finally convinces her younger sister, Riley, to take her to Paw & Maw, the swallow-themed studio where she works. As Judy's fascination with the world of swallow-themed has grown, she and her husband have become devoted fans of several of the studio's performers, and she can't resist the chance to see the place for herself.

The reception area is surprisingly polished, if a little unsettling. Along one wall sits a series of glass trophy cases displaying the cleaned and mounted skulls of former prey actors, each accompanied by a plaque commemorating their "final performance." Judy gives the exhibit a distracted glance before signing the extensive consent forms required for entry.

Despite Riley's warnings, Judy slips away in search of her husband's favorite actor, hoping to surprise him with an autograph. Unfortunately, he isn't alone. The two performers greet their unexpected admirer with warm smiles and offer to continue the meet-and-greet somewhere more private, leading the eager fan toward one of the studio's darker unused rooms."
